newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Rally in U.S. debt futures to resume soon.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Rally in U.S. debt futures to resume soon.

text.p: Most U.S. debt futures remained slightly lower at midsession, but technical analysts said the rally in both September T-bonds and December Eurodollars should resume soon.
"We expect within the next couple of days for September to break above 113-31/32," Steve Boyajian, director of technical analysis at MMS International, said.
September set a seven-month high on Monday at 113-31/32.
Short-term overbought conditions are the only negatives gripping T-bonds, with RSIs and stochastics having turned higher within September's uptrending channel from April.
September T-bonds have been trending higher since setting a nine-month low at 105-30/32 on April 11, but the strength of the uptrend has been in question until recently.
"The fact that September penetrated a key 61.8 percent Fibonacci retracement level means the market is no longer in a corrective phase," Boyajian said.
September T-bonds rose to 112-24/32 on June 20, retracing 61.8 percent of the bond contract's decline on a monthly continuation chart from its November peak of 116-28/32, Boyajian said.
Boyajian expects a rally to carry September to the 75-percent retracement level of 114-08/32 in the near term.
Michael Krauss, chief technical strategist at Chase Securities Inc, noted several proprietary surveys that showed money and portfolio managers were not excessively long U.S. Treasuries.
"Despite the length and the magnitude of the rally since April, managers haven't gotten excessively long, which has given T-bonds a residual bid," Krauss said.

Kruass looks for yields on the 30-year cash T-bond to stall at 6.50 percent in the near term, which is close to 115-00 in the September T-bond futures contract. He projected that yields would rise no more than 6.62 percent, which is roughly equivalent to 113-09/32 in September bonds.
September T-bonds held above that support level in early trade. The contract set a daily low at 113-12/32, near minor support at 113-11/32.
The spread between December and March Eurodollars continued to narrow in early pit trade. The spread fell to four basis points from five on Monday.
"It should continue to narrow," Boyajian said. "But I wouldn't expect it to invert. Few people have said the next Fed move will be an ease."
December Eurodollars traded below Monday's high of 94.08 and well above support at 94.02. ((Chicago derivatives desk (312)408-8750))
